io_driver_functions.notes: Chip-ID dispatch-table initializer: calls FUN_0802e2fc to probe ID, matches against a table at _DAT_0802e800, installs 6 function-pointer globals, tail-calls through an unrecovered jump table. No static caller found in the decompiled corpus.
Flash manufacturer/device ID probe: unlock handshake 0xAA/0x55 then 0x90 (autoselect), reads IDs via func_0x0802ec5c including a literal read at 0xE000000, then issues 0xAA/0x55/0xF0/0xF0 reset/exit.
Halfword block-copy scratch helper used by the sector-erase routine before issuing Flash commands.

Sector erase: guarded to sector indices 0-15 (consistent with a 64 KiB chip as sixteen 4 KiB sectors). Issues 0x80/0xAA/0x55/<addr>:0x30 sector-erase command sequence, then polls completion via func_0x0802ec54. No static caller found.
Byte/word program primitive; optional bank-select via external func_0x0802e2d8 when detected chip size == 0x20000 (128 KiB); tail-calls func_0x0802ec54 with address (offset<<shift)+0xE000000.
Program primitive variant, same shape as 0x0802e550.
Program primitive variant, same shape as 0x0802e550/0x0802e61c.
Write-with-retry wrapper (3 attempts) around func_0x0802ec50 + FUN_0802e61c. No static caller found in decompiled corpus.
Write-with-retry wrapper (3 attempts) around func_0x0802ec50 + FUN_0802e6b4. No static caller found in decompiled corpus.

NOT save-specific: generic unsigned-division-with-trap compiler runtime routine (calls func_0x0802ed18 on divide-by-zero). Included in the original MMIO-seed set due to address proximity only; flagged here to avoid misclassification as save logic.

open_questions: What routine outside the 133-function decompiled set assembles save records and invokes the traced Flash driver? It is only reachable via an unrecovered indirect jump table.
Is there any checksum/CRC in this title's save path, or does it rely solely on the chip-level write-verify-retry wrappers (0x0802e74c/0x0802e790) for integrity? No evidence found either way.

Do blocks A, B, C (offsets 0x1000/0x2000/0x3000) represent three redundant full copies, three difficulty/world-specific stage tables, or something else? Differing record counts (35/35/30) argue against simple full-copy redundancy but are not conclusive.
What do the HAG/SHO/ROY 3-letter tags mean, and why is ROY unmirrored while HAG/SHO are mirrored at +0x9000?
Is the 0x00000007 value at 0x6D98 a counter, a flag, or a default game parameter?
